title: Sorting and Limiting
summary: ORDER BY sorts results ascending (default) or descending (DESC); LIMIT caps row count; OFFSET skips rows for pagination.
learningObjectives: Apply the concept in a small program
Predict program output by reading code

sections.content: ORDER BY sorts results ascending (default) or descending (DESC); LIMIT caps row count; OFFSET skips rows for pagination.
Sort multiple columns: ORDER BY last_name, first_name. Sorting happens after WHERE filtering.
Key points: always use LIMIT on big tables, OFFSET pagination gets slow deep — prefer keyset/cursor pagination, and ties in sort need a unique tiebreaker column.
Try this variation — change a value, predict the output, then run it:
sections.codeExample:
SELECT name, score FROM players
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 10;
-- experiment: modify a value above and predict the new output
